text:
Nina C: FYI provisioning of new GPU racks in ap-southeast-1 is stuck at instance-init. nodes hit "attach volume: decrypt failed" and never register. saw ~12 failures across two AZs starting 04:03 UTC.
Trevor M: that sounds like keystore/KMS issue. Any KMS errors in control-plane logs?
Omar H: yes, control-plane shows repeated 504s to keystore-proxy and some TLS verify errors: "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority". suspect our new fw egress rules dropped the internal keystore CA path.
Priya S: we rolled out the tightened egress policy last night to lock down outbound to trusted subnets only. It allows keystore.internal:443 and iam.internal:443, but someone changed keystore.hostnames -> keystore-prx.internal (CNAME) and the fw uses TLS SNI mappings so it didn't match.
Nina C: hmm. nodes need to contact keystore-prx.internal for disk decrypt (LUKS) during early boot. if SNI mismatch -> blocked by fw.
Omar H: node logs: 
```
Apr 07 04:05:12 init: INFO fetching key from https://keystore-prx.internal/v1/decrypt
Apr 07 04:05:13 init: ERR tls handshake error: remote error: tls: unknown certificate authority
Apr 07 04:05:13 cloud-init: ERROR cannot decrypt root volume, aborting
```
Trevor M: options:
- revert the egress rule (fast but lossy)
- add keystore-prx.internal to allowlist (tight and targeted)
- proxy keystore traffic via internal ALB in allowed CIDR (ops heavier)
Priya S: also noticed audit exporter to logging-edge was queuing since it couldn't reach the shipper. risk: if we revert fw, we open too much. prefer targeted allowlist and a quick canary.
CostsBot: note: adding an ALB route will add ~ $0.025/hr + small data costs in region. Reverting FW affects security posture.
Nina C: canary plan: add keystore-prx.internal + cert chain CAs to fw allowlist in one AZ's warm-pool only, boot 4 nodes. If they join and audit exporter drains, expand.
Omar H: add extra logging for tls handshake and capture server cert chain to verify CA. we might need to update our CA bundle on proxies.
Priya S: terraform snippet to add hostname rule (we use host-based egress):
```hcl
resource "egress_rule" "allow_keystore_prx" {
  name = "ap-se1-keystore-prx-allow"
  vpc  = "vpc-zzzz"
  host = ["keystore-prx.internal"]
  ports = [443]
  ttl   = "2h"
}
```
Trevor M: one more constraint: regulatory requires keystore traffic to never traverse a public NAT. confirm host resolves to private IPs only.
Nina C: yes verified: keystore-prx.internal resolves to eni IPs in privnets.
Omar H: launching canary now (tag: egress-canary=keystore). I'll tail kernel and init logs, and watch node-agent for decrypt success.
OpsBot: Incident created INF-9001 "ap-se1 gpu node decrypt fails after egress tighten" assigned to @Omar H and @Priya S. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9001 :warning:
Priya S: rule applied to az-a warm-pool. starting 4 canary instances.
Omar H: canaries reached decrypt step and completed at 04:22 UTC, kubelet registered. audit exporter initial backlog drained over ~6 minutes. marking canary success. :white_check_mark:
Nina C: next steps: update fw rules to include keystore-prx.internal and add automated SNI-to-host mapping check in our fw pipeline. open PR to update CA bundle on proxies as well.
Trevor M: I'll kick off quick runbook change: preflight check for host CNAMEs and cert chain before egress-tightening. low-effort guardrail.
CostsBot: cost delta for targeted host allowlist is negligible. ALB approach is more durable but adds ops. Recommend allowlist + CA bundle update first.
Priya S: agreed. I'm posting the terraform diff and will schedule the CA bundle rollout during the low-traffic window tonight.
Nina C: thanks all. closing once PR merged and runbook updated.
